decisions.decision: THE DECISIVE MEASUREMENT: the four gaps are not four repairs. Two are already closed in the shipped tree and the dogfood exercise ALREADY CONTAINS their closing probes, written verdict-free and handed to this task by name. Measured at a602b98. (i) cap-human-input-request: `grep -rn 'domain.RequirementStartFraming' --include='*.go' . | grep -v _test.go` returns 2 lines, one comment and one issuer, internal/application/framing.go:191; internal/domain/model.go:475 admits that command from RequirementCaptured only and :496 admits RequirementNeedInput from framing, active or evaluating, so the precondition V2-022 called unreachable is reachable through Service.StartFraming and POST /v1/requirements/{id}:start-framing (internal/api/api.go:660 and :766). The probe at internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go:1070-1212 already walks captured -> framing -> needs-input -> ready over the real base URL and asserts the reason class, both options with impacts, stopped_scope, continuing_scope, the SAME requirement_id resumed, status ready and an unchanged Backlog row count -- every clause of the declared success condition. (ii) cap-backlog-visibility's recorded ground E22-11 is closed: internal/store/firestore/store.go:637 documentIDCursor passes the bare collection-relative id (V2-079) and the probe at live_dogfood_test.go:576-687 pages to exhaustion at page_size=1 over the cursor the route itself issues, covering every capture exactly once. BOTH probes log verbatim that they issue no verdict and that 'the verdict and its evidence_ids belong to the M5 re-dogfood'. THEREFORE the shape is: two real repairs (the Backlog's missing declared confirmation items with the repository filter, and one owner document route), one closure that needs NO production change at all (cap-repository-registration), and one verdict-and-observation pass over all four.
decisions.rationale: Treating the four symmetrically was the alternative and it is rejected on measurement. It would have produced four repairs where two are already paid, and the two that are paid are paid IN THE EXERCISE FILE ITSELF -- so a symmetric design would have rewritten probes that already assert more than the declaration asks, and would have needed either a sixth M5 task (forbidden by section 12.7) or a boundary widening it did not need. Reading the two verdict-free probes is also what fixes the task's true difficulty: the hard part is not reaching the states, it is that cap-backlog-visibility's declaration names eight confirmation items and its own failure condition makes a missing one a failure, which no record has ever measured.

decisions.decision: THE VERDICT IS JUDGED AGAINST outcome_conditions QUOTED VERBATIM, AND THE FOUR DECLARATIONS DIFFER IN HOW MUCH OF observable_result THEY IMPORT -- measured, not chosen. From contracts/release-contract/foundation-capabilities.json: cap-repository-registration's failure is '登録が拒否される、または識別情報・実行可否のいずれかが表示されない', which names exactly two of the six observables its observable_result lists, so the other four (Preview/Stable state, policy, Runners and AI resources -- all three of which internal/application/repository.go:558-575 renders as ObservedNotImplemented with a stated reason) are reported as measured absences and do NOT change the verdict. cap-backlog-visibility's failure is '一覧が取得できない、または必須の確認項目が欠落する', which DOES import the confirmation items, so every item of its observable_result is verdict-bearing. cap-user-documentation's success is '利用中channel/versionに対応する文書が完全に参照でき、実挙動との差異がない', two clauses, both verdict-bearing. cap-human-input-request's success is 'Requirement詳細にneeds-inputの理由、選択肢、影響、停止/継続範囲が表示され、回答後に同じRequirementが再開する', which the existing probe already asserts clause by clause. The rule: quote success and failure into each check, judge against them, and report every observable_result element the declaration does not import as a measured presence or absence with its reason.
decisions.rationale: This is the rule V2-022 itself applied when it recorded E22-7 as 'a shortfall and not as a failure of the success condition', but it applied it without deriving it, so nothing stopped the same record from never enumerating cap-backlog-visibility's eight items at all. Deriving the rule from the declaration makes the asymmetry between the four capabilities a measurement instead of a judgement, and it is the only way a `passed` verdict can be defended item by item against a gate that reads the declaration.

decisions.decision: THE RULING ON cap-repository-registration: IT IS A PRODUCT GAP M5 OWNS, NOT A DECLARATION-DERIVED DEFERRAL. Three independent measurements settle it and each is a command. (1) Its declared external systems are exactly GitHub, Git, Firestore and owner UI, and its declared providers list is EMPTY -- measured by reading external_dependencies for all twelve capabilities out of contracts/release-contract/foundation-capabilities.json. Section 8.3 admits exactly two deferral grades, 'declares Google Cloud Run -> D1' and 'declares codex and opencode, unauthenticated on this machine -> M6', and NEITHER is derivable from that declaration: no Cloud Run, no codex, no opencode. (2) Section 8.3's reverse constraint applies directly. The recorded reason was 'this task's declared side-effect surface excludes every forge and every remote' -- a property of V2-022's own scope, i.e. the observation 'we could not reach it', which section 8.3 forbids as a source of deferral. (3) The systems it names are measurably present and usable here, so there is no external-unavailable ground either: `gh --version` reports 2.92.0, `gh auth status` reports logged in to github.com as wakuwaku3 with repo scope, `git --version` reports 2.43.0, and the repository already carries read-only live exercises for both -- internal/runner/forge_live_test.go:42 TestForgeReachabilityLive against owner wakuwaku3 and name agentic-loop-foundation, and internal/runner/git_live_test.go:45 TestGitCloneLive. Section 12.9 reaches the same classification and this packet's measurement is independent of it.
decisions.rationale: The boundary in section 8.3 is one-directional and this is the side that is easy to launder: 'GitHub was not contacted' reads like an external constraint. It is not one -- it was a scope decision of a different task, and the forge is authenticated on this very machine. Recording it as a deferral would have made the deferral set eight instead of seven and would have satisfied M5 by relabelling, which is exactly the move section 8.3 exists to refuse. The measurement that settles it is the authentication state, because it converts 'could not' into 'did not', and only 'could not, by declaration' defers.

decisions.decision: THE SEVEN DEFERRALS ARE DERIVED FROM THE DECLARATION FILE BY A TEST, NOT ASSERTED IN PROSE. Measured partition of the twelve declarations by external_dependencies: FOUR declare Google Cloud Run -- cap-preview-operation, cap-stable-promotion, cap-loop-control, cap-loop-self-update; THREE declare providers codex and opencode -- cap-autonomous-resolution, cap-shared-resource-allocation, cap-provider-operation; FIVE declare neither -- cap-repository-registration, cap-requirement-intake, cap-backlog-visibility, cap-human-input-request, cap-user-documentation. 4 + 3 + 5 = 12, exactly section 12.9's table, re-derived. This partition becomes a new deterministic test that internal/contracts owns, so the classification is re-executed by make check at every judging commit (G6a) instead of being an argument inside a live record. The test asserts the three sets by name and asserts the REVERSE constraint too: no capability in the M5-owned five declares Cloud Run, codex or opencode. The machine half stays in the live record: codex and opencode are unauthenticated here, which .agents/v2/task-state/V2-028.json already records as measured on 2026-08-26 with 'Not logged in' and '0 credentials', and which the exercise re-measures at observation time.
decisions.rationale: Section 8.3 says the deferral is 'not a judgement but a measurable fact derivable from the capability's declaration'. If that is true then it belongs in a test, and if it is in a test the gate never has to take the record's word for it. Putting the reverse constraint in the SAME test is what stops the set from growing later: adding an eighth deferral would require either editing a declaration (prohibited here) or turning the test red.

decisions.decision: HOW `passed` IS HONEST -- and the answer is forced by the schema, which has no word for it. Measured: contracts/schemas/evidence.json constrains checks[].status to the enum passed, failed, skipped, and there is no 'ineligible' member; result is passed, failed or partial. So ineligible-by-declaration must be expressed inside that enum. It is recorded as `skipped`, one check per deferred capability, named exactly the capability id, whose summary quotes the declared external system that derives the deferral and names the machine measurement. That choice is not a convenience: G7 forbids counting a skipped test as a pass, which is precisely the property wanted -- a deferred capability must never be readable as an exercised one -- and internal/contracts/capability_evidence_test.go's reverse rule fires only on `passed`, so a skipped check correctly writes no evidence_ids and the capability keeps its empty array. The record is therefore: twelve capability-named checks, FIVE passed, SEVEN skipped, ZERO failed, and result passed. G7's separate demand that a live record show the test actually ran is satisfied at the layer it is about: the go test verdict must show zero SKIP lines for the exercise, recorded with the exact grep pattern beside the number, and the seven skipped CHECKS are a record-layer classification of subtests that all ran and all recorded observations. Stating that separation is mandatory, because conflating the two layers is how a skipped test becomes a pass.
decisions.rationale: The schema is the authority and it was measured rather than assumed; a design that invented a status string would have failed internal/contracts. Choosing `skipped` over `passed`-with-a-caveat is the whole difference between a record that is honest and a record that is relabelled: `passed` on a deferred capability would satisfy the forward bijection, would demand evidence_ids, and would claim an exercise that never happened. Choosing it over `failed` is section 8.3's rule. And keeping all twelve names present means a gate reading the record can enumerate the closure rather than infer it from absence.

decisions.decision: THE UNDER-REPORTING GUARD IS HARD-SCOPED TO A TASK ID THAT WILL NEVER ISSUE AGAIN, AND GENERALISING IT IS PROVABLY NON-BREAKING. Measured: internal/contracts/capability_evidence_test.go:227 calls capabilityEvidenceReverse(claims, records, "V2-022") and :214-219 only loads records whose TaskID equals V2-022. The forward rule (a cited record must carry that capability's passed check) does reach any record. The reverse rule -- 'a record that reports a capability passed must be cited back', which the file's own header calls 'the more valuable half' because it 'makes it impossible to exercise a capability successfully and then under-report it' -- does not reach this task's records at all. So without a change, V2-095 could exercise a capability, report it passed, omit it from the contract, and make check would stay green. The generalisation is measured to be safe: scanning all 171 index entries for checks whose name equals one of the twelve capability ids finds EXACTLY ONE record, ev-v2-022-release-live-dogfood, with 12 such checks of which 1 is passed. Every other record, including all five provider-live ones, carries zero capability-named checks. So removing the task-id scope adds coverage and zero new violations.
decisions.rationale: This is the guard that makes the whole verdict trustworthy, and it was measured to be pointed at the past. Extending it to a two-element set would work and is rejected: the next live record would need a third edit, and a guard that must be edited to keep working is a guard that will stop working. Removing the scope is safe by measurement rather than by hope, and the measurement is a one-line command a reviewer can re-run. The negative control is what keeps the removal from being vacuous -- a synthetic record reporting an uncited passed capability must still produce exactly one violation.

decisions.decision: THE RECORD M5 STANDS ON IS OUTSIDE THE CHECK MEANT TO GUARD IT, AND MY BRIEF WAS WRONG ABOUT THIS. Measured: internal/contracts/provider_preflight.go:160 is `if !strings.HasPrefix(component, "provider-live-")` and it is the ONLY prefix test; `grep -rn 'release-live' --include='*.go' .` returns ZERO lines. So component release-live-dogfood is NOT selected by CheckProviderPreflightLedger, and the two invariants that check enforces -- an artifact_refs entry with artifact_id provider-preflight whose sha256 equals the preflight record's own bytes, and approval.approved_at strictly before observed_at -- are not enforced on the one record M5's G2 must read. This is the same silent-escape shape section 9.6 records for component `runner`, live today on the M5 ground. DESIGN CONSEQUENCE: issue TWO records, exactly as V2-022 did. ev-v2-095-release-live-dogfood (component release-live-dogfood) is M5's G2 ground and carries the twelve capability verdicts; ev-v2-095-provider-live-claude-dogfood (component provider-live-claude-dogfood) is selected by :160 and therefore has both invariants MECHANICALLY enforced, and it carries the channel-break-and-resume witness that roadmap M5's completion condition 2 needs. The release-live record carries the identical provider-preflight artifact_refs entry voluntarily and states in its own check that the check does not reach it, with the digest recomputed and compared inside the record. Extending :160 is NOT done here: internal/contracts/provider_preflight.go is prohibited and the reach gap is recorded as a finding in row (3).
decisions.rationale: The brief said the prefix admits release-live- and it does not; taking that on trust would have left the binding unenforced on the exact record the gate reads, which is how V2-080's record fell out of the check it was written for. Two records is not duplication: the provider-live one exists so the binding is enforced by a machine, and the release-live one exists because section 8.2 names release-live-dogfood as M5's required component. Discharging the binding by construction in the release-live record, and saying plainly that no check verifies it, is the honest form of a guard that cannot reach you -- and it also means extending :160 later would find the record already compliant.

decisions.decision: cap-backlog-visibility's EIGHT DECLARED CONFIRMATION ITEMS, ENUMERATED AGAINST THE ACTUAL WIRE SHAPE, AND EACH MISSING ONE ALREADY EXISTS SOMEWHERE THE CODE DISCARDS. Measured against internal/application/readmodels.go's RequirementView (:104-121, eight fields: requirement_id, status, version, increment_ids, text, requested_by, repository_id, captured_at) and the queue summary. PRESENT: 要求内容 (text), 現在の利用者向け状態 (status), 関連Repository (repository_id, :114), 実行中/停滞中/自動回復中/人間対応待ちの区別 (the domain status enum contains active, waiting, recovering and needs-input at internal/domain/model.go:95-99). AGGREGATE ONLY: 進行中Incrementと進捗 -- the row carries increment ids and no status; queueSummary carries by_increment_status. ABSENT FROM BOTH: 優先度とその根拠; Preview/Stable反映状況; 次のaction. Each absent one is already computed and thrown away: nextAction(status, incs, execs) exists at readmodels.go:309 and is used only on the detail view at :303; domain.Requirement.StableSnapshot is a field of the aggregate the list already reads and is projected nowhere; and allocationReport (allocation.go:596-641) already calls scheduler.Decide at :625 over one bounded page of at most scheduler.MaxCandidates = 100 and keeps only a reason histogram, discarding plan.Decisions' per-candidate RequirementID, Rank, Score, Assigned, Reason and Inputs (internal/scheduler/decision.go:110-121). CLOSURE, with no new port and no new store query: project StableSnapshot onto the row (zero reads); reuse the two EXISTING batch ports IncrementsForRequirements and ExecutionsForIncrements (internal/application/ports.go:123-124) once per page, capped at MaxPageSize ids in total with the existing Truncated idiom, and feed the EXISTING nextAction verbatim; and project plan.Decisions into queueSummary. The eight items are then satisfied jointly by listRequirements and queueSummary, which is exactly what the declared preview_exercise names.
decisions.rationale: The declaration's failure condition imports the confirmation items, so a `passed` verdict has to survive an item-by-item reading, and V2-022's check never performed one -- it measured the cursor, the page bound, the full page and the summary counters, and no record has ever enumerated the eight. Deriving each missing item's home from code rather than designing a new read model is what keeps this bounded: three of the four are projections of values already in hand, and the fourth reuses two ports that already exist for the detail view. The alternative -- adding a priority field to domain.Requirement -- is refused: it edits the domain, and section 5 assigns the PriorityAssessment connection to V2-030 in M7.

decisions.decision: 優先度とその根拠 IS A PROJECTION, NOT NEW MACHINERY -- AND THE GAP LEDGER'S ROW THAT SAYS OTHERWISE IS FALSE AT THIS COMMIT. .agents/v2/DECLARATION-GAP.md L92b records 'control planeが優先順位を管理する | ABSENT | domain.PriorityAssessment 型が存在しない' with the evidence 'grep -rn PriorityAssessment internal --include=*.go | grep -v _test.go -> internal/scheduler/decision.go:44,64,66,107 のcomment 4件のみ'. Re-running that EXACT command at a602b98 returns 13 non-test lines, including internal/domain/model.go:66 `type PriorityAssessment struct`, internal/scheduler/priority.go:128 multiFactorScore(a domain.PriorityAssessment, age int64) and internal/scheduler/scheduler.go:70 Assessment *domain.PriorityAssessment. The type exists and the scheduler consumes it. What is actually absent is narrower and is measured here: internal/application/allocation.go:457-467 builds every scheduler.Requirement with no Priority and no Assessment, so the score in force is the legacy age-only branch, and ScoreInputs.UsedAssessment is false for every candidate. THEREFORE the honest projection reports rank, assigned, the reason from scheduler.AllReasons' closed seven, and the score inputs actually used INCLUDING UsedAssessment false -- which states in the response that the multi-factor assessment did not feed the ranking. A Requirement beyond the scheduler's candidate bound carries no Decision and is reported as an explicit absence with its reason, never as a plausible rank, following the idiom internal/web/owner.html:7 already states.
decisions.rationale: A designer who trusted the ledger would have concluded the item was unreachable and either failed the capability or edited the domain. Re-running the ledger's own command is what turned an ABSENT into a projection. Reporting UsedAssessment false rather than hiding it is the point: it is a truthful rationale that also says what the rationale is NOT, which is the only way to report a priority the product intends to be multi-factor while the code ranks by age.

decisions.decision: THE DOCUMENT ROUTE'S ALLOWLIST IS DERIVED FROM THE ASSEMBLED BUNDLE, NOT CHOSEN, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES IT SAFE. Measured: the gap ledger's row L253-259 is TRUE at this commit -- `grep -rn --include='*.go' 'docs/stable|docs/preview' internal/api internal/web | grep -v _test.go` returns 0, and the exercise measures GET /owner/docs/preview/index.md and GET /docs/preview/index.md both answering 405 (E22-10). internal/web embeds only owner.html, owner.css and owner.js (internal/web/web.go), so the documents are not in the binary; they are members of the release bundle, resolved from a root. The route therefore serves EXACTLY the documentation-role member set of the bundle assembled from the configured root -- the same five paths internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go:701-709 lists as dogfoodDocSet and the same set release.AssembleFromRoot resolves for that role -- and refuses every other path. Because the allowlist is the assembled member set, there is no path to traverse: a request naming anything outside it is refused before any file is opened, and the set is recomputed from the tree rather than written down. An index answer names the channel from release.ResolveChannel and the version from the assembled contract, so 'the documents corresponding to the channel and version in use' is answered by construction. With NO root configured the route answers the same 503 shape /v1/release/state answers, never a default root.
decisions.rationale: cap-user-documentation's only declared external system is the owner console, so 'the owner reads the working tree instead' cannot be the answer, and it was V2-022's measured reason for the failure. The dangerous version of this route is a path-joining file server; the safe version is a lookup in a set the release package already computes for the promotion gate, which also guarantees the served documents are precisely the ones whose digest the candidate is bound to. Preserving 503 on an unconfigured root is not politeness: internal/application/release_surface.go:17-23 already records why a defaulted root is a lie, and V2-091's A17 asserts that exact behaviour, so a default here would turn its test red.

decisions.decision: THE 503 HALF OF cap-user-documentation BELONGS TO V2-091 AND MUST NOT BE WIRED A SECOND TIME. Measured at a602b98: Service.AttachReleaseObserver (internal/application/release_surface.go:51) and NewSourceReleaseObserver (:121) have ZERO non-test callers -- every hit is in release_surface_test.go or provider_compatibility_test.go -- so internal/api/api.go:962 answers 503 release_observer_not_configured, which is the gap ledger's row at DECLARATION-GAP.md:110 and the second half of V2-022's A8 reason. dp-v2-091 d13 and wo-v2-091 A17 wire it, in internal/application, behind explicit environment variables, and V2-091 is in this task's dependencies. So this task does NOT add a wiring path. It (a) measures V2-091's constructor and environment variable names at its own baseline, because they are not knowable at design time, (b) starts the dogfood process WITH that configuration so the route the documents describe actually answers, (c) reuses the SAME configuration for the document route so there is one release-source configuration and not two, and (d) re-measures GET /v1/release/state and reverses the inverted assertion at live_dogfood_test.go:812-818, which currently FAILS ON PURPOSE if the route ever returns 200. If the wiring is absent when this task starts, STOP and escalate; do not wire it here.
decisions.rationale: Two producers of a release source is the same defect class as two producers of a caller identity, and V2-091 has the boundary. The inverted assertion is the mechanism that makes the handoff safe -- the previous task left a test that fails the moment its deviation is repaired, so the repair cannot land silently and the verdict cannot be inherited. Honouring that means reversing the assertion deliberately, in the task the probe names, rather than deleting it.

decisions.decision: THE DOCUMENT EDITS ARE BUNDLE-MEMBER EDITS, THEY MUST PRECEDE THE OBSERVATION, AND ONE ASSERTION IN THE EXERCISE MAKES A NATURAL EDIT FATAL. Measured: four passages record deviations this task repairs and become false the moment it lands -- docs/preview/capabilities.md:80 (the 503 measurement), :150 (cap-user-documentation's two reasons and 証跡なし), and docs/preview/stable-diff.md:33-34 and :64-65 (the unwired observer and the missing document route). docs/preview/**.md are documentation-role bundle members, so editing them moves the docs digest and the BundleDigest; therefore every doc edit lands BEFORE the observation commit. THE TRAP, measured at live_dogfood_test.go:773-780: the exercise counts fenced code blocks across all five documents and FAILS if the total is not zero. Documenting a new route is exactly the place an implementer writes a fenced example. Do not. Two more measured constraints on the same edit: release.VerifyCapabilityAnchorBijection requires the anchor set of capabilities.md to equal the contract's twelve ids in BOTH directions, and release.VerifyRequiredSections requires stable-diff.md to carry all four RequiredPreviewSections. docs/preview/index.md and docs/stable/index.md are PROHIBITED on purpose, so a release-marker edit is a build failure rather than a discovery.
decisions.rationale: Section 12.5 forbids declaring more than is implemented, which cuts both ways here: leaving the four passages standing would make the documents describe behaviour that no longer exists, and that difference is literally the second clause of this capability's success condition. Naming the zero-code-block assertion as a trap is worth more than a general instruction, because it is the single most likely way a correct documentation edit turns the live exercise red -- after the provider invocations have been spent.

decisions.decision: THE COMMIT ORDER IS THE DESIGN, BECAUSE ONE BUNDLE MEMBER CANNOT PRECEDE THE RECORD THAT FORCES IT. Measured: internal/contracts/capability_evidence_test.go's forward rule requires that every evidence id written into a capability's evidence_ids resolve in the index AND that the record it names carry a check whose name is exactly that capability id with status passed. So contracts/release-contract/foundation.json's evidence_ids cannot be written before the records exist, and the records cannot exist before the observation. THEREFORE foundation.json is the ONE bundle member whose edit necessarily follows the observation, and it is the one entry of the published exercise file set's excluded_with_reason group that is not itself an evidence artifact. The exclusion is bounded by a measurement rather than by an argument: `git diff <observation> <judging> -- contracts/release-contract/foundation.json` must show ONLY additions inside evidence_ids arrays, with the release string, the capability id list, every status field and the field order byte-identical, and that diff is transcribed into the record. Everything else lands before the observation. The order is: (1) the two records carrying the A1 boundary table and the A2 baseline; (2) the preflight record; (3) the deterministic repairs and their proofs; (4) the document edits; (5) gofmt, vet and the full non-live suite green; (6) the observation, at a commit anchored by a pushed refs/live-observations ref; (7) the records, the artifact, the index and foundation.json's evidence_ids.
decisions.rationale: V2-022's commit B did the same thing and got away with it only because its derived file set was go-list-only, so foundation.json was never in the judged set at all. Publishing a set that includes what the exercise reads at run time -- which it must, since the exercise reads the contract, the documents and the preflight record -- makes that circularity explicit, and the only honest handling is an exclusion whose scope is measured to the shape of the diff. V2-080 established exactly this technique for the evidence artifacts; this extends it to one contract field and bounds it.

decisions.decision: SIZING IS BY RESERVATION COUNT, AND THE GAP BETWEEN RESERVATIONS AND SETTLEMENTS IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN TRANSIENT -- WHICH CORRECTS THE PREMISE I WAS GIVEN. Measured from the five ledgers: internal/runner/costledger.go:364 refuses when len(Entries)+1 exceeds max_invocations, so a RESERVATION counts whether or not it settles. Entry states: V2-017 9 settled + 2 reserved = 11 of 16; V2-022 16 + 7 = 23 of 24; V2-063 8 + 3 = 11 of 12; V2-075 9 + 3 = 12 of 12; V2-080 8 + 2 = 10 of 48. Seventeen of sixty-seven reservations, 25.4 percent, never settled. V2-022's purpose histogram is decisive: autonomous-resolution 9, graceful-stop-live-child 7, resume-after-channel-rollback 7, and ALL SEVEN graceful-stop entries are `reserved` -- that purpose kills the child, so it can never settle. So one full run of TestFoundationPreviewLocalDogfood is exactly THREE reservations of which two can settle, V2-022 ran the exercise SEVEN times (seven stop-and-resume pairs), and its overhead was 2 extra autonomous-resolution reservations, not the 'one to three transient failures per observation' the ledger notes claim. Money: costledger.go:353-360 blocks 1.00 USD per UNSETTLED reservation and min(actual, reserved) per settled one, so V2-022 stood at 1.008563 + 7.00 + 1.00 = 9.008563 of 20.00, 45 percent, while at 96 percent of its count. Money is far from binding, but NOT because settlements are cheap -- because unsettled reservations at 1.00 each are still only a third of the ceiling.
decisions.rationale: Section 9.5 already corrected itself once here and the correction is still incomplete: it attributes the whole reservation-to-settlement gap to transient provider failure. The purpose histogram shows most of it is one purpose that cannot settle by construction. That matters for sizing, because a design that budgets for 'retries' underestimates a fixed per-run cost, which is how V2-063 and V2-075 both ended at exactly their ceiling. Showing the monetary arithmetic matters for the same reason: the brief's 0.07-0.11 USD per invocation is the settled figure, and it is not the figure the ceiling is computed against.

decisions.decision: THE STABILITY PROBE IS RESTRUCTURED, BECAUSE THE ONLY SUBTEST THAT EVER DISAGREED IS THE ONE WHOSE CAPABILITY IS NOW DEFERRED. Measured from ev-v2-022-release-live-dogfood's A19 check: two runs at the same commit on identical candidate digests disagreed on exactly one of seventeen subtests, cap-autonomous-resolution, whose run-1 failure was a real claude invocation returning failure class provider-transport; A19 was recorded failed for that reason, the record became partial, and the tie was left UNBROKEN because the ledger stood at 23 of 24 and a third full run could not be admitted. cap-autonomous-resolution declares codex and opencode, so under section 8.3 it is now ineligible-by-declaration and its check is skipped, not failed. THEREFORE: run the full exercise TWICE on the identical final commit and record both verdicts; a disagreement confined to a subtest whose capability is deferred is recorded as an observation with both transcriptions and does not make the record partial; a disagreement on any of the five M5-owned capability subtests is a FAIL-CLOSED STOP and is escalated, not retried; and the budget admits a third run so a tie can be BROKEN rather than left standing. The subtest still invokes the real claude CLI -- that invocation is the environment-grade witness and the provider record's substance -- and at least one settled invocation carrying a provider-issued session_id must exist across the run, or the provider record may not claim a real CLI was reached.
decisions.rationale: Requiring two runs is what made V2-022 partial, and dropping to one run would discharge G5 trivially while learning nothing. The measured fact reframes it: the flake lives entirely in the provider path, and that path's capability no longer bears a verdict, so two runs now cost their invocations and can no longer be defeated by the one thing that defeated them. Budgeting the tie-breaker in advance is the direct remedy for the failure A19 reported about itself -- it had the right procedure and no headroom to finish it.

decisions.decision: cap-repository-registration CLOSES WITH ZERO PRODUCTION CHANGE, AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT. The mechanism is complete: POST /v1/repositories, GET /v1/repositories, GET /v1/repositories/{id} and the runner-role POST /v1/repositories/{id}:observe all exist (internal/api/repositories.go:1-18 and :95-104); internal/application/repository.go:576 computes Executability from the submitted Observation through domain.RepositoryExecutabilityFrom; internal/runner/forge.go and internal/runner/git.go both exist with read-only live exercises. What was missing was only that V2-022's declared side-effect surface excluded every forge, so no Observation was ever produced and executability stayed `unobserved` with the reason 'the Control Plane holds no forge client and never probes the forge itself' -- which is correct behaviour, not a defect. So the closure is entirely inside the exercise: resolve the real gh executable and the real git through the EXISTING clients, read the real repository wakuwaku3/agentic-loop-foundation read-only, POST the resulting bounded Observation to :observe with the runner token, and assert executability leaves `unobserved` with the forge identifiers recorded. internal/runner/** is PROHIBITED: the clients must be used exactly as they are, because a change to them would mean the closure was widened rather than reached. The declared 'no external resource is changed without permission' clause is proven the same way the existing live exercises prove it -- the only argv the read path can produce is the read-and-version pair, and nothing creates, modifies or deletes any branch, ref, tag, PR, issue or repository.
decisions.rationale: This is the gap that looked largest in the brief and is measurably the smallest, and finding that out is what keeps the task inside one boundary. The temptation is to give the Control Plane a forge client; that would contradict the design the code states in a comment at repositories.go:17-18 and would put a network call on an owner read path. Reaching the forge from the exercise, as a Runner would, is the shape the aggregate was built for -- and it is why G3 item 1's demand for real GitHub identifiers can be met without a single line of production code.

decisions.decision: THE GRADE, AND THE SENTENCES THAT MAY NOT BE WRITTEN. The environment class is preview-local: the owner's own machine, the real cmd/control-plane process, the real claude CLI, the real gh and git CLIs, the Firestore emulator as canonical store. Under G3 item 2 that IS the real-environment grade for conditions about the Loop's own observable behaviour, and it is not a substitute for anything. Under G3 item 1 the GitHub and Git halves of cap-repository-registration are satisfied by real identifiers -- gh version, resolved absolute executable path, the forge node id and the observed default branch. What preview-local cannot establish stays unclaimed: the IAP boundary, scale-to-zero, real Firestore permissions and contention, the deploy path and any Cloud Run fact, all of which belong to D1. FORBIDDEN VERBATIM in both records and in any summary: 'this was observed on Cloud Run', 'the deployed environment', 'a Stable promotion occurred', 'all twelve capabilities were exercised', 'all capabilities passed', and any sentence asserting a capability whose check is skipped. Also forbidden: describing the seven skipped capabilities as failed, or the four M5-owned gaps as deferred.
decisions.rationale: Section 8.2 records a coordinator getting the grade question wrong and paying a gate failure for it, and section 8.1's correction 2 records a judge accepting one occurrence as a safety proof. A record that will be read as M5's sole admissible ground is the worst possible place to overclaim, and this one adds two more real CLIs to the feeling of production. A forbidden-sentence list is grep-able; a caveat is not.

decisions.decision: DETERMINISM IS ACCEPTANCE EVERYWHERE EXCEPT THE PROVIDER PATH, AND THERE THE DURATION IS AN OBSERVATION. Every new or modified test: no fixed sleep, no wall-clock timer, no goroutine, no randomness; clocks injected; every wait a bounded deadline poll reusing the existing dogfoodPoll idiom at internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go:250; -race on the whole non-live suite. The two batch reads added to the list page and the Decision projection added to the summary are pure functions of values already read, so their tests are table tests over decoded inputs with no clock at all. The live run is not deterministic and is not pretended to be: every duration measured during the observation is recorded as an observation and never asserted as a threshold, and the two-run pair is the disclosure mechanism rather than a determinism claim.
decisions.rationale: Commit 56ee097 on main is the repository's own record of fixed-timeout waits being replaced by bounded polls, and a live exercise that starts processes is exactly where a sleep reappears. Saying which parts are deterministic and which are not, rather than claiming determinism uniformly, is what keeps the record readable: a recorded duration that is not an assertion cannot become a flaky gate later.

risks: r1. THE HIGHEST RISK IS THAT A REPAIR LANDS AFTER THE OBSERVATION. Eleven of this task's source paths are inside the exercise's own 88-path compiled set, including internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go itself, so any edit after the observation forces re-observation under G6b regardless of its nature -- and V2-022 was caught by exactly this, needing a whitespace-only gofmt fix to internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go after its runs. Mitigation: gofmt, go vet and the whole non-live suite must be green and committed BEFORE the first provider invocation, the commit order in d13 is an acceptance item, and the intersection is measured at the end rather than assumed.

r2. THE SECOND HIGHEST IS A `passed` THAT IS ACHIEVED BY NARROWING. Every gap has a cheap version: serve one document instead of the channel's set, report a priority field that is really an index, filter by reading the page and dropping rows so page_size silently lies, or POST a hand-written forge Observation without contacting GitHub. Each would pass a suite that only asserts the positive case. Mitigation is structural: the document allowlist is the assembled member set and internal/release is prohibited so it cannot be hand-written; the priority projection must carry UsedAssessment false; the filter must go through the existing port and internal/store is prohibited; and the Observation must carry a forge node id and a default branch that came from the real read.

r3. THE DEFERRAL SET COULD GROW TO COVER A PRODUCT GAP. The pressure is real: if one of the four proves harder than measured, moving it to the deferred side turns a red record green. Mitigation: the partition is a test that names all three sets and asserts the reverse constraint, so an eighth deferral requires either editing a declaration -- contracts/release-contract/foundation-capabilities.json is prohibited -- or turning that test red.

r4. THE LEDGER HALTS MID-OBSERVATION. Three of the five existing ledgers ended at or one below their ceiling, and reaching a threshold is a stop, not a failure, so the remedy is another new record and another task -- which section 12.7's budget forbids. Mitigation: the ceiling is derived from the measured per-run reservation cost times twice the planned run count, the never-settling graceful-stop reservation is counted as structural rather than as retry headroom, and the monetary ceiling is computed against unsettled reservations at 1.00 USD each rather than against the settled per-invocation figure.

r5. V2-091's WIRING MAY NOT MATCH WHAT THIS PACKET ASSUMES. Its constructor name, its environment variable names and whether attachment is conditional are all unknowable at design time. Mitigation: they are A2 baseline measurements, the document route must reuse the same configuration rather than add a second, and an absent wiring is an escalation rather than a second wiring path.

r6. THE DOCUMENT ROUTE COULD BECOME A FILE SERVER. A path-joining handler under /owner/ that reads from a configured root is a directory traversal and an information disclosure on the owner surface. Mitigation: the served set is a lookup in the assembled documentation-role member set, refusal happens before any file is opened, and the negative half of v10 asserts both an out-of-set path and a traversal attempt.

r7. THE SUMMARY'S NEW PROJECTION COULD MAKE AN OWNER READ UNBOUNDED. queueSummary already runs the scheduler over one bounded page; adding a per-candidate projection is bounded by the same page, but adding a second page, a second Decide call or a per-row read would not be. Mitigation: no new read in allocationReport at all -- the projection consumes plan.Decisions, which is already in hand -- and the measured read and write counts are recorded against internal/quota's reservations.

r8. THIS TASK MOVES V2-080's M3-LIVE RECORD OUT OF G6b FRESHNESS. Measured: three of this task's paths -- internal/application/allocation.go, internal/application/readmodels.go and internal/application/release_surface.go -- are inside the 103-path set published at .agents/v2/evidence/artifacts/V2-080-live-exercise-files.json. V2-018 is terminal (failed) and no M3 gate task is pending, so nothing is invalidated today, but any future M3 re-judgement will need another provider-live-claude observation. Recorded as a fact in row (3) so a later gate is not surprised; no task is proposed.

r9. THE TWO-RUN PAIR COULD DISAGREE ON A CAPABILITY THAT MATTERS. The measured provider-transport failure rate makes a disagreement inside the provider subtest likely enough to plan for, and d15 handles that case; a disagreement inside one of the five M5-owned subtests would mean a repair is non-deterministic, which is a design failure and not a retry candidate. Mitigation: that case is a fail-closed stop and an escalation, written into constraints, and the deterministic repairs are all pure projections of values already read, which is the property that makes such a disagreement structurally unlikely.

r10. A CORRECT DOCUMENTATION EDIT COULD TURN THE LIVE EXERCISE RED AFTER THE INVOCATIONS ARE SPENT. The zero-fenced-code-block assertion, the anchor bijection and the four required sections are all evaluated inside the live exercise over the real doc set. Mitigation: the document edits land before the observation and the full non-live suite plus one gated dry run of the deterministic subtests must be green first; the three invariants are named individually in v14 rather than left to a general instruction.
